evidence.senderRole: the pool paying the token out to a buyer
evidence.recipientRole: the counterparty of the taxed transfer
evidence.poolRole: a constant-product pool holding this token, used here to show that pool-side transfers are taxed
evidence.requestedAmountDerivation: the transfer is internal to a swap, so amount is reconstructed as transferToRecipient + transferToTaxDestination; the exact floor identity below confirms the reconstruction.
evidence.computation: One transfer of 61067270056521333217 emits two Transfer events with the same sender: 60250800655865642992 to 0x40abed95df97953088c7de4f83c7c4395a2410f8 and 816469400655690225 to 0x167d87a906da361a10061fe42bbe89451c2ee584. fee = floor(amount * 1337 / 100000); transferToRecipient = amount - fee reproduces BOTH emitted amounts EXACTLY, so the measured tax is 8164694006556902250000/61067270056521333217 bps == 133.7 bps up to the one-base-unit floor residue.
evidence.corroboration: the same floor identity at 133.7 bps holds on 34 independent two-leg transfers of this token found by replaying eth_getLogs, 8 of which have the pool 0xe477a79cb22153beb165e3921f63334413e3b597 as an endpoint (6 pool->user, 2 user->pool).
evidence.reproduce: eth_getLogs on address 0x30c8cf6b46aa4df3f9fbc2857aca92f10a6cad7f at block 78446572 for topic0 0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef, then group by (transactionHash, topics[1]) and look for the two legs sharing this sender.

note: Fee-on-transfer token: a taxed transfer emits TWO Transfer events with the SAME sender -- 98.663% of the amount to the intended recipient and 1.337% sent to the fee collector 0x167d87a906da361a10061fe42bbe89451c2ee584. Both legs are in the receipt, so the split is reproducible from eth_getLogs alone with no tracing. The fee is a floored integer division, so the realised rate equals 133.7 bps up to a rounding residue of at most one base unit; the exact rational for the cited transaction is in evidence.taxBpsExactRational. NOTE the rate is not a round number: it is exactly 133.7 bps, reproduced as a floored integer division and not rounded to a neater value. Confirmed on 34 independent two-leg transfers, 8 of them with the pool 0xe477a79cb22153beb165e3921f63334413e3b597 as an endpoint, so pool-side transfers ARE taxed -- which is what makes the token unsafe as a routing hop rather than merely unusual. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE -- the destination pool receives only 98.663% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) as TERMINAL OUTPUT -- no next pool and no K() revert, but the user receives 98.663% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating the minAmountOut slippage promise (delivered < quoted). Both modes are unsafe.
